html:
SMTO-EXE-0220 — SMTO couldn't reach Docker on the Gateway computer

GUID: 15ab05fc-a201-5add-b4c4-c6ee19af2ebf
Slug: docker-engine-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • SMTO asked the Gateway computer to work with Docker but got no usable answer, either from the Gateway (SMTO's helper program on that computer) or from Docker itself. SMTO uses this message only when no change had started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, find the Gateway you picked for this conversation, and select Check connection. Docker requests run only on that Gateway, so SMTO has to reach it first.
  2. On that computer, make sure Docker is installed and running, for example that Docker Desktop is open or the Docker service is started. If Docker isn't running, the Gateway has nothing to talk to.
  3. Ask the person who set up the Gateway to confirm it points to the right Docker connection and that its user account can use Docker. The Gateway only uses the one Docker connection it was set up with and never picks another.
  4. When Check connection succeeds and Docker is running, ask SMTO to continue. No change had started, so asking again is safe once the connection works.

What success looks like

  • Check connection succeeds, and SMTO can list the Docker containers on that Gateway.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't install or start a second copy of Docker to get around this; the Gateway only uses the one it was set up with.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server's Docker request to the selected Gateway failed, or the Gateway could not connect to, or read a response from, its configured local Docker Engine socket before any change was recorded.

What this means

  • The local Engine request failed socket/HTTP/JSON handling before any mutation was recorded, or the controller's Docker Gateway operation/control route failed. These are distinct transport boundaries. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The local Engine request failed socket/HTTP/JSON handling before any mutation was recorded, or the controller's Docker Gateway operation/control route failed. These are distinct transport boundaries.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify controller-to-Gateway versus Gateway-to-local-Engine failure using phase and retained operation facts.

How to fix it

  • Check Gateway reachability (Settings › Setup › Gateways › Check connection) and the Gateway log for /docker/operation. On the Gateway host, confirm the Docker Engine is running and that the socket named by GATEWAY_DOCKER_ENDPOINT (default unix:///var/run/docker.sock) exists and is usable by the Gateway account, for example by running docker version as that user; DOCKER_HOST and CLI contexts are ignored.
  • Restore the failed Gateway or local Engine connection and inspect original operation state before another mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Verify the selected Gateway account can access its explicitly configured local Docker socket.

How to verify the fix

  • The same verified Gateway can reach its configured local Engine, and any original operation is settled.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
